title: Comets
description: Comets are the leftovers of the outer solar system: ice, dust and organic molecules, kept cold since the planets formed. Jupiter-family comets were thrown inward by Jupiter and come round every few years; long-period comets fall in from the Oort cloud, far out. One number from the orbit, Tisserand's parameter, tells which: between 2 and 3, Jupiter's family. Rosetta found comet 67P's water three times richer in deuterium than our oceans; Stardust found glycine, an amino acid, in comet Wild 2's dust. Unlocks a comet mission.

puzzle.goal: For an orbit of semi-major axis a and eccentricity e in Jupiter's plane, write Tisserand's parameter T with respect to Jupiter, whose semi-major axis is aJ.
puzzle.name: Tisserand parameter
puzzle.form: aJ / a + 2 * sqrt ( a / aJ * ( 1 - e ^ 2 ) )
puzzle.expr: aJ / a + 2 * sqrt ( a / aJ * ( 1 - e ^ 2 ) )
puzzle.ask: Find T for aJ = 5.2 AU, a = @{a} AU and e = 0.64 (comet 67P).
puzzle.method: In the frame turning with Jupiter, the Jacobi constant is kept through an encounter; far from Jupiter it reduces to this.
